ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r1.claim: The statement that unbelievers' prayer is futile is apparently spoken by Hell's keepers; another view makes it God's message to Muhammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال من كلام الخزنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r2.claim: These future events are expressed in past tense to convey certainty that they will occur.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p264/r2.anchor: وجاءت هذه الأخبار معبرا عنها بلفظ الماضي الواقع لتيقن وقوعها

STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.claim: Verses 10–20 warn of the disbelievers’ Hereafter; this sets up the extended Moses and Pharaoh account, centered on a believer in Pharaoh’s House challenging opposition to Moses.
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.anchor: Vv. 10–20 then tell of the place of the disbelievers in the Hereafter

THALABI:v8p277#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p277#2/r1.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v8p277#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the idols cannot answer anyone in this life or the next, so they have no answered invocation.
THALABI:v8p277#2/r1.anchor: يعني لا يستجيب لأحد في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة

THALABI:v8p277#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p277#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p277#2/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the claim as saying the idols have no answered prayer.
THALABI:v8p277#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: ليست له دعوة مستجابة

THALABI:v8p277#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p277#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p277#2/r3.claim: Another view says idols are invoked in this world but deny their worshippers in the next, since they never called people to worship them or claimed divinity.
THALABI:v8p277#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: ليس له دعوة في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة إلا عبدوها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.claim: The Moses–Pharaoh account warns Quraysh, encourages Muhammad and his companions to endure trials until victory, and profiles a Pharaoh’s family believer as a lesson for Quraysh and hesitant sympathizers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.anchor: A specific part of the account of Moses (sws) and the Pharaoh is recounted so that a reminder can be sounded

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.claim: The Moses and Pharaoh story supports the prior claim that a people rejecting their messenger are destroyed despite worldly grandeur, and assures the Prophet and companions to persevere in their duty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.anchor: when a messenger is sent to a nation and it denies him, then it is necessarily destroyed however much it may be superior

IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r5.claim: Abu Amr lightens the sīn in plural forms attached to a two-letter pronoun, such as رسلنا and رسلكم; a report has him lighten على رسلك, but another says he reads it heavy, as do the other readers generally.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p194/r5.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو ما أضيف إلى مكني على حرفين مثل ﴿ رسلنا ﴾

STUDYQURAN:40:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r2.claim: Instead of interceding, the angels remind Hell’s inhabitants that they had received guidance but rejected God’s messengers.
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r2.anchor: Rather than interceding, the angels remind the denizens of Hell that they had in fact been granted guidance before

STUDYQURAN:40:49/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r3.claim: Their belated affirmation cannot avert or alleviate punishment, and their supplications cannot help; other passages voice the same too-late plea.
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r3.anchor: their now belated affirmation can do nothing to forestall or alleviate their punishment; nor can their supplications

STUDYQURAN:40:49/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r4.claim: Even if the disbelievers were sent back, they would return to what they had been forbidden.
STUDYQURAN:40:49/r4.anchor: even if they were sent back, they would return to the very thing they had been forbidden

BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r5.claim: The keepers answer only after a delay.

BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r6.claim: The hamza is interrogative and the waw coordinates the question with the omitted sense ‘did you not take notice of this’; the messengers’ coming is described as continual in worldly life.
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r6.anchor: الهمزة للاستفهام ، والواو للعطف على مقداري ألم تنبهوا

BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r7.claim: The messengers brought clear proofs of the evil end of disbelief and sins, to establish the damned’s guilt and reproach them for wasting the chance to pray and disabling its means of acceptance.
BURSEVI:v8p145#4/r7.anchor: بالحجج الواضحة الدالة على سوء عاقبة ما كنتم عليه من الكفر والمعاصي

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r1.claim: They admit that the messengers brought proofs, but say they rejected them, as in Sūrat al-Mulk.

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r2.claim: The keepers tell them to pray themselves because it would be implausible for the keepers to do it for them; the command is meant to extinguish hope and expose the truth, not promise an answer.
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r2.anchor: ولم يريدوا بأمرهم بالدعاء أطماعهم في الإجابة

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r3.claim: The genitive can make الدعاء the disbelievers’ own prayer, or the prayer of others offered on their behalf.
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r3.anchor: فالمصدر مضاف إلى فاعله ، أو وما دعاء غيرهم لهم

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r4.claim: Their prayer is futile and void of effect because they make it at the wrong time.
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r4.anchor: في ضياع وبطلان الإيجاب ؛ لأنهم دعوا في غير وقته

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r5.speaker: الجمهور
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r5.claim: The majority forbids saying that a disbeliever’s prayer is answered, citing this verse and arguing that disbelief means the person does not know God or has invalidated belief by describing Him improperly.

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r6.claim: Some allow that a wronged person’s prayer is answered even if the person is a disbeliever, interpreting kufr here as ingratitude; Satan’s prayer for respite, which was granted, is also evidence, and Bursevī says the permissive ruling is followed.
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r6.anchor: فمحمول على كفران النعمة وجوزه بعضهم

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r7.claim: Bursevī also adduces God granting Satan’s request for respite as evidence that a disbeliever’s prayer can be answered.
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r7.anchor: فقال الله تعالى : إنك من المنظرين

BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r8.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r8.claim: Saʿdī’s poem illustrates the futility of idolatry: after an idol fails its devotee for years, God grants the need when the desperate man collapses at the temple.
BURSEVI:v8p145#5/r8.anchor:
قال الشيخ سعدي :
مغى در بروى از جهان

TABRISI:40:50/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:50/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:50/r10.claim: In the question, the omitted subject of كان is القصة, and the following clause about messengers explains that story.
TABRISI:40:50/r10.anchor: التقدير أو لم تك القصة وتأتيكم رسلكم تفسير القصة فاسم كان مضمر

TABRISI:40:50/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:50/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:50/r11.claim: The guards ask whether messengers had brought clear proofs of divine unity and prophethood, since the sinners disbelieved and stubbornly resisted.
TABRISI:40:50/r11.anchor: أي الحجج والدلالات على صحة التوحيد والنبوات أي فكفرتم وعاندتم

TABRISI:40:50/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:50/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:50/r12.claim: The people admit that messengers and proofs came, but say they denied them and rejected the messengers' prophethood.
TABRISI:40:50/r12.anchor: جاءتنا الرسل والبينات فكذبناهم وجحدنا نبوتهم

TABRISI:40:50/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:50/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:50/r13.claim: The guards tell the inhabitants to pray for themselves because the guards may pray only with permission and have not received it.
TABRISI:40:50/r13.anchor: أي قالت الخزنة فادعوا أنتم فإنا لا ندعوا إلا بإذن ولم يؤذن لنا فيه

TABRISI:40:50/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:50/r14.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:50/r14.claim: One alternative takes the guards' words as contemptuous dismissal.
TABRISI:40:50/r14.anchor: وقيل: إنما قالوا ذلك استخفافا بهم

TABRISI:40:50/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:50/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:50/r15.claim: Another alternative says the guards tell them to pray for woe and destruction.

TABRISI:40:50/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:50/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:50/r16.claim: The unbelievers' supplication is futile because it brings them no benefit.
TABRISI:40:50/r16.anchor: أي في ضياع لأنه لا ينتفع به

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:49-51/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:49-51/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:49-51/r2.claim: After the inmates acknowledge that messengers brought them proofs, the keepers tell them to pray for themselves; the keepers will not pray for them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:49-51/r2.anchor: أي: فادعوا أنتم إذا، فإنا لن ندعو الله لكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:49-51/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:49-51/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:49-51/r3.claim: The invocation of the disbelievers is futile and fruitless because it does not benefit them.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r2.claim: Those who followed the powerful instead of freely choosing their beliefs and actions are cast into Hell with them and ask the leaders to remove even part of the fire; the leaders know they can save no one, and the requesters likely know this too, so the question exposes their helplessness (Razi).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r2.anchor: Bu ikincilerden, dünyadayken inanç ve eylemlerini kendi özgür iradeleriyle seçmek yerine, baskıcı kesimin talepleri istikametinde hareket edenler, bu tutumları sebebiyle âhirette diğerleriyle birlikte cehenneme atılınca

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r3.claim: For true freedom and salvation, people must choose beliefs and conduct freely rather than become followers of wealthy, influential, immoral deniers; once God judges, no one can rescue another, and even angels refuse their pleas.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r3.anchor: İnsanlar, hasbelkader yüksek bir ekonomik güç, toplumsal ve siyasî statü elde etmiş olan inkârcı ve erdemsiz kesimlerin, baskın grupların uydusu olmak yerine, kendilerini Allah karşısında sorumlu duruma düşürecek inanç ve davranış konularında özgür bireyler olarak seçimlerini hür iradeleriyle kendileri yapmalıdırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r4.claim: People must seek salvation before Judgment Day, when no one can help except by God’s will; in this life they should resist inner desires and dominant misleaders, heed God’s messenger and clear truths, and follow his pure way of life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:47/r4.anchor: İnsan kendi kurtuluşunu arama görevini kıyamet gününe bırakmamalıdır; çünkü o zaman Allah’ın dilemesi dışında kimse kimseye yardımcı olamayacaktır. Şu halde insan, kurtuluş çarelerini dünyada aramalı

BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.claim: For ten occurrences, many readers and linguists prefer stopping at بلى because it answers the preceding statement without syntactic dependence on what follows; some allow beginning there.
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.anchor: أحدها ما يختار فيه كثير من القراء وأهل اللغة الوقف عليها لأنها جواب لما قبلها غير متعلق بما بعدها

BURHAN:v1p407#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r5.claim: In the question to the condemned, the dropped nūn marks the messengers' gradual ascent from sense evidence to reason and remembrance, and from ignorance to certainty.
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r5.anchor: جاءتهم الرسل من أقرب شىء فى البيان الذى أقل من مبدأ فيه وهو الحس إلى العقل إلى الذكر

ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r1.claim: Classical commentators take the keepers' reply as a refusal to intercede, effectively telling the doomed sinners to pray for themselves if they can.
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r1.anchor: According to the classical commentators, this answer implies no more than a refusal on the part of the "keepers of hell" to intercede

ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r2.claim: Asad instead reads "pray, then" as telling sinners to invoke the false worship objects and values to which they once attributed a share in divinity and see whether those can help.
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r2.anchor: we have here an indirect allusion to the sinners erstwhile, blasphemous devotion to false objects of worship and false values

ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r3.claim: Asad's reading is supported by the next clause: the deniers' prayers were deluded in earthly life, whereas such delusions have vanished by Judgment Day.
ASAD-NOTES:40:49#n34/r3.anchor: This interpretation finds support in the next sentence, which speaks of the delusion (dalal) inherent in the prayers of "those who deny the truth"

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r13.speaker: الزركشي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r13.claim: Al-Zarkashi explains that the messengers began with the nearest proofs accessible to the senses, then raised people from ignorance toward reason, remembrance, and certainty.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r13.anchor: وجاء في (البرهان) للزركشي أن حذف النون في نحو هذا قد يكون "تنبيهاً على صغر مبدأ الشيء وحقارته

NASHR:v1p451/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p451/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p451/r4.claim: Eight words with final hamza after alif are written with the hamza on waw without disagreement; the listed examples include شركاء in al-Anʿām, نشاء in Hūd, and دعاء in Ghāfir.
NASHR:v1p451/r4.anchor: فالمضمومة منها ثمان كلمات كتبت الهمزة فيها واوا بلا خلاف، وهي (شركاء) في الأنعام

QIRAAT-ER:40:50:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:40:50:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:40:50:6#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on sīn compresses rusulukum to ruslukum, tightening the sound while preserving referent and syntactic role.
QIRAAT-ER:40:50:6#1/r1.anchor: Canonical sukūn reading compresses the plural from rusulukum to ruslukum

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r1.claim: The keepers ask whether messengers repeatedly came in worldly life with clear proofs of the evil outcome of disbelief and sins, reproaching the inmates for seeking more time and disabling the grounds for response.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r1.anchor: في الدنيا على الاستمرار بالحجج الواضحة الدالة على سوء مغبة ما كنتم عليه من الكفر والمعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r2.claim: They admit the messengers came and that they disbelieved them, as another verse states explicitly.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r2.anchor: أي أتونا بها فكذبناهم كما نطق به قوله تعالى : ( بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r3.claim: The fa is explanatory ellipsis: since the inmates admit this, the keepers tell them to pray themselves, because the keepers cannot pray for those who acted as they did.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r3.anchor: فصيحة أي غذا كان الأمر كذلك فادعوا أنتم فإن الدعاء لمن يفعل فعلكم ذلك مستحيل صدوره عنا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r4.claim: The alternative says the keepers were not authorized to pray for such people; al-Ālūsī rejects it because it does not explain the fa’s attribution of refusal to the inmates’ conduct and suggests permission could have changed matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r4.anchor: وقيل : في تعليل امتناع الخزنة عن الدعاء : لأنا لم نؤذن في الدعاء لأمثالكم وتعقب بأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r5.claim: The keepers’ command is meant to make the inmates despair, not to raise hope of an answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r5.anchor: ولم يريدوا بأمرهم بالدعاء إطماعهم في الإجابة بل إقناطهم منها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r6.claim: The keepers say the disbelievers’ prayer is futile and will not be answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r6.anchor: أي في ضياع وبطلان أي لا يجاب فهذه الجملة من كلام الخزنة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r7.claim: An alternative takes the final sentence as God’s report to Muhammad.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r7.anchor: وقيل : هي من كلامه تعالى إخبارا منه سبحانه لرسوله محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r8.claim: Some infer that a disbeliever’s prayer is never answered and that disbelievers cannot join the rain prayer; al-Ālūsī limits the verse to their prayer on Judgment Day, noting that worldly requests may be granted, whatever one calls that outcome.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p76/r8.anchor: واستدل بها مطلقا من قال : إن دعاء الكافر لا يستجاب وأنه لا يمكن من الخروج في الاستسقاء والحق أن الآية في دعاء الكفار يوم القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r4.claim: The keepers ask whether messengers had come to them with clear proofs; the condemned admit that they had.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r5.claim: The keepers tell them to pray for themselves, refusing to pray on their behalf because they know the punishment will not be reduced.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r5.anchor: أنتم إذا ربكم، إنا لا ندعو لكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p151#2/r6.claim: The disbelievers' prayer is futile, misguided, and of no benefit to them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r1.claim: The guardians invoke the messengers' clear proofs to make the inmates acknowledge the evidence and rebuke them for wasting their opportunity to pray and neglecting means of response.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r1.anchor: أرادوا به إلزامهم للحجة وتوبيخهم على إضاعتهم أوقات الدعاء وتعطيلهم أسباب الإجابة

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r2.claim: The guardians say they themselves dare not pray because they have not been permitted to intercede for people like the inmates, thereby making them despair of an answer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r2.anchor: فإنا لا نجترىء فيه إذ لم يؤذن لنا في الدعاء لأمثالكم، وفيه إقناط لهم عن الإجابة

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r3.claim: The disbelievers' prayer is fruitless and will not be answered; the statement further extinguishes their hope of an answer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:50-51/r3.anchor: ضياع لا يجاب، وفيه اقناط لهم عن الإجابة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r6.claim: The guardians expose why the damned are cast aside and unworthy of a hearing: they had received messengers bearing clear proofs.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r6.anchor: الجاعل لهم في محل الاطراح والسفول عن التأهل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r7.claim: The guardians rebuke them for failing to use reason and for wasting the time when answered prayer might have helped.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r7.anchor: إلزامنا لهم الحجة وتوبيخا وتنديما بتفويت أوقات الدعاء المجاب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r8.claim: The nūn is omitted from تك, while the imperfect تأتيكم depicts the messengers' successive, repeated coming.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r8.anchor: بإسقاط النون مع التصوير للحال بالمضارع

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r9.claim: Their messengers were human beings from among them, so they should have listened; people are more receptive to their own kind.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r9.anchor: أي الذين هم منكم فأنتم جديرون بالإصغاء إليهم والإقبال عليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r10.claim: The messengers came with proofs clearer than anything else.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r10.anchor: أي التي لا شيء أوضح منها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r11.claim: The people of Hell admit that the messengers did come to them with such proofs.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r12.claim: The guardians tell them to pray now, whether to God or to God's human messengers, angels, or others; alternatively, they tell them to stop because no one will hear them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r12.anchor: أي أنتم الآن الله أو أهل الله من رسل البشر أو الملائكة أو غيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r13.claim: The disbelievers are those who veil their faculties of reason from the light of reason supported by sound transmission.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r13.anchor: الساترين لمرائي عقولهم عن أنوار العقل المؤيد بصحيح النقل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r14.claim: Their prayer goes nowhere, as their worldly deeds did: this life is the Hereafter's field, and the harvest there is of the kind planted here.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p522/r14.anchor: أي ذهاب في غير طريق موصل كما كانوا هم في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p159#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p159#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p159#2/r8.claim: On the second analysis, the pronoun refers to the people of Hell generally, not Pharaoh’s family: the following scene mentions their guardians and plural messengers, while Pharaoh had only Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p159#2/r8.anchor: وضمير { يتحاجون } غير عائد إلى { ءال فرعون } ( غافر : 46 ) لأن ذلك يأباه قوله : { وقال الذين في النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r1.claim: The guardians’ confirmatory question exposes the inmates’ blameworthy choice, makes them regret wasted chances of salvation, rebukes them, and recalls the warning of everlasting punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r1.anchor: وجواب خزنة جهنم لهم بطريق الاستفهام التقريري المراد به : إظهار سوء صنيعهم بأنفسهم إذ لم يتبعوا الرسل حتى وقعوا في هذا العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r2.claim: The waw coordinates the guardians’ words with the inmates’ request by عطف التلقين, as if the omitted reply should continue with this reminder; compare 2:124.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r2.anchor: والواو في قوله : { أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم } لم يعرج المفسرون على موقعها . وهي واو العطف عطف بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r3.claim: The command follows naturally from the admission of the messengers’ proofs under either analysis of the preceding waw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r3.anchor: على ذلك ظاهر على كلا التقديرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r4.claim: The final clause may be the guardians’ conclusion, warning that the inmates’ prayer is futile, or a divine parenthetical conclusion; the waw is parenthetic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r4.anchor: وجملة { وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال } يجوز أن تكون من كلام خزنة جهنم تذييلا لكلامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r5.claim: Bayyināt are clear proofs and explicit calls to follow guidance; the inmates admit the messengers brought them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r5.anchor: والبينات : الحجج الواضحة والدعوات الصريحة إلى اتباع الهدى . فلم يسعهم إلا الاعتراف بمجيء الرسل إليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r6.claim: After the admission, the guardians decline to intercede and leave the inmates to themselves: since they turned away from messengers by their own choice, they may manage their own affairs now.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r6.anchor: إلى إيكال أمرهم إلى أنفسهم بقولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r7.claim: The command means permission or equal treatment, and highlights the error in asking; the saying is that whoever chooses its cool must bear its heat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p165/r7.anchor: فإن ( من تولى قرها يتولى حرها ) ، فالأمر في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r1.claim: The added verb كون signals that messengers’ coming is an established reality; لم supplies the past-time negation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r1.anchor: وزيادة فعل الكون في { أولم تك تأتيكم } للدلالة على أن مجيء الرسل إلى الأمم أمر متقرر محقق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r2.claim: Ḍalāl means loss or going astray, originally missing the road, as in 32:10.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r2.anchor: والضلال : الضياع ، وأصله : خطأ الطريق ، كما في قوله تعالى : { أإذا ضللنا في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r3.claim: The prayer of disbelievers does not benefit them or get accepted. Whether the words are the angels’ or God’s, the generic annexed noun makes the denial universal across times and places.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r3.anchor: والمعنى : أن دعاءهم لا ينفعهم ولا يقبل منهم ، وسواء كان قوله : { وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال } من كلام الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r4.claim: Apparent rescues after disbelievers pray (6:63–64; 10:22–23) do not show their prayers were honorably accepted; they expose their ingratitude after God saves them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r4.anchor: فظاهر أن هذه لا تدل على استجابة كرامة ولكنها لتسجيل كفرهم ونكرانهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r5.claim: An apparently fulfilled disbeliever’s prayer may coincide with the prayer of righteous people rather than be answered for the disbeliever’s sake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r5.anchor: وقد يتوهم في بعض الأحوال أن يدعو الكافر فيقع ما طلبه وإنما ذلك لمصادفة دعائه وقت إجابة دعاء غيره من الصالحين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم؛ أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r6.claim: In a Muslim hadith from Abu Hurayra, the Prophet describes a disheveled traveler raising his hands to God whose food, drink, and nourishment are unlawful, then asks how his prayer could be answered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r6.anchor: وقد جاء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استبعاد استجابة دعاء المؤمن الذي يأكل الحرام ويلبس الحرام في حديث مسلم عن أبي هريرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r7.claim: The Qur’an says God saved them, not that He answered their prayer: their rescue may have been decreed already or their prayer may have coincided with believers’ prayers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p166/r7.anchor: ولهذا لم يقل الله : فلما استجاب دعاءهم ، وإنما قال : فلما نجاهم ، أي لأنه قدر نجاتهم من قبل أن يدعوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r11.claim: The keepers rebuke them by asking whether messengers had brought proofs; the unbelievers admit they had, and the keepers mockingly tell them to pray for themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r11.anchor: فراجعتهم الخزنة على معنى التوبيخ لهم. والتقرير: أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات فأقر الكفار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r12.claim: One group takes the closing statement about futile prayer as the keepers’ words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r12.anchor: وقالت فرقة: وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال هو من قول الخزنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r13.claim: Another group takes the statement as God’s report to Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p563/r13.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هو من قول الله تعالى إخبارا منه لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r3.claim: The keepers remind them that messengers established proof; after the inmates admit it, the keepers tell them to pray for themselves, refuse to help or seek their release, and say praying will not change anything.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r3.anchor: أي: أوما قامت عليكم الحجج في الدنيا على ألسنة الرسل؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r4.claim: The disbelievers' supplication is futile: it is not accepted or answered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p149/r4.anchor: إلا من ذهاب، لا يتقبل ولا يستجاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r1.claim: The keepers of Hell are the attendants charged with torturing its inhabitants.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r2.claim: Mentioning Jahannam rather than using a pronoun heightens terror; the name may also derive from جهنام, a deep well, and the poet al-Nābigha was called جهنام for his deep knowledge of poetry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن جهنم هي أبعد النار قعرا ، من قولهم : بئر جهنام بعيدة القعر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r3.claim: The worst and most rebellious unbelievers may be in this fire; they deliberately ask its keepers because angels assigned to them might be especially likely to have their prayers answered through their closeness to God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r3.anchor: وفيها أعنى الكفار وأطغاهم ، فلعل الملائكة الموكلين بعذاب أولئك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r4.claim: The keepers’ question forces proof and rebukes them for having let opportunities to pray and supplicate pass and for neglecting the conditions that make prayers answerable.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r4.anchor: إلزام للحجة وتوبيخ ، وأنهم خلفوا وراءهم أوقات الدعاء والتضرع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r5.claim: The keepers say they cannot dare to intercede except for someone who is not an evildoer and when permission is granted, before the final judgment separates the groups.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r5.anchor: فإنا لا نجترىء على ذلك ولا نشفع إلا بشرطين : كون المشفوع له غير ظالم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r6.claim: The command to ask is an expression of despair, not hope: if a close angel’s prayer goes unheard, a disbeliever’s will fare worse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p176/r6.anchor: ولكن للدلالة على الخيبة ؛ فإن الملك المقرب إذا لم يسمع دعاؤه

MUQATIL:40:48-50/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:48-50/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:40:48-50/r4.claim: The keepers remind them that messengers from among themselves brought clarifying proofs; the people admit this, and the keepers say to pray, since disbelievers' prayers only stray.
MUQATIL:40:48-50/r4.anchor: يعنى رسل منكم { بالبينات } يعنى بالبيان { قالوا بلى } قد جاءتنا الرسل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r1.claim: After a long interval, the keepers rebuke them; “was there not” refers to the story or occasion, and the following words explain it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r1.anchor: اى الخزنة توبيخا لهم بعد مدة طويلة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r3.claim: The disbelievers answer yes; the keepers then mock them, telling them to call for themselves, since their prayer will not be answered.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r3.anchor: اى الكفار ﴿ بلى قالوا ﴾ اى الخزنة تهكما بهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r4.claim: The statement that disbelievers' prayer is futile may be Allah's own speech or may continue the keepers' taunt.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p77#3/r4.anchor: بطلان وهو من قول الله تعالى ويحتمل ان يكون من كلام الخزنة
